components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action button for primary workflows
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary actions, filter triggers, dropdown triggers
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid var(--border); cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M18 6L6 18M6 6l12 12"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); padding: 8px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete actions — used sparingly, always Crimson
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: var(--destructive); color: var(--destructive-foreground); padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 150ms; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text inputs with optional icon prefix
components.css: .ds-input-wrapper { position: relative; } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 8px 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Badge
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.4; background: var(--secondary); color: var(--secondary-foreground); } .ds-badge-outline { background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-badge-destructive { background: var(--destructive); color: var(--destructive-foreground); }

components.name: Table Row
components.description: Repository list items with hover and selection states
components.css: .ds-table-row { transition: background 150ms; } .ds-table-row:hover { background: var(--accent); } .ds-table-row[data-state="selected"] { background: var(--accent); } .ds-table-row td { padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }

components.name: Floating Action Bar
components.description: Contextual toolbar for bulk operations — the only elevated surface
components.html: 3 repositories selected

narrative.overview:
OctoManager's visual identity is rooted in the workbench metaphor — a clean, organized space where every tool has its place and nothing gets in the way. The aesthetic is clinical precision meets warm craft: the cold efficiency of a terminal married to the tactile satisfaction of well-made tools.

The system operates on a strict monochromatic Zinc palette, trusting that restraint in color forces better hierarchy through typography, spacing, and weight. Color appears only where it must: destructive actions (red), active states (blue), and language indicators (tiny dots). Everything else lives in the grayscale spectrum, letting content and structure do the talking.
keyCharacteristics: Monochromatic Zinc palette with no decorative color
Soft, tactile component feel with subtle elevation
Typographic hierarchy driven by weight and size, not color
Minimal shadow vocabulary — one level for elevated surfaces
Keyboard-first interaction patterns (Cmd+K search, Esc to clear)

rules.name: The Zinc Rule
rules.body: All surfaces, backgrounds, and text use only the Zinc scale. No decorative colors appear anywhere in the interface. The sole exceptions are Crimson for destructive actions and Switch Active for toggle states — their rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through font-weight, not color. Bold text is always interactive or a heading; regular text is always content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The single shadow level appears only on surfaces that float above the base layer. Interactive elements never have shadows.

dos: Do use font-weight to signal hierarchy: bold for interactive/heading, regular for content
Do keep the Zinc palette sacred — no decorative colors anywhere
Do use the single shadow level only for floating surfaces (cards, modals, action bars)
Do maintain 4px grid alignment for all spacing values
Do use Ghost buttons for toolbar actions and secondary navigation
Do show destructive actions in Crimson, never in any other color
donts: Don't add shadows to buttons, inputs, or table rows
Don't use color to distinguish interactive states — use background shifts and borders
Don't exceed 12px border-radius on any component
Don't add decorative gradients, patterns, or textures to backgrounds
Don't use blue, green, yellow, or any accent color outside the Switch component
Don't create visual hierarchy through color when font-weight can do the job
